claims.text: A new predictive approach can accurately estimate lattice and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr separately.
Incorporating atomic-scale complexity and separate transport studies will improve predictive performance.
The new approach will be at least 20% more accurate than earlier approaches.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a BCC crystal structure in the stated initial state.
Atomic-scale complexity in HfNbTaTiZr includes variations in atomic mass and force constants.
Lattice distortions are a relevant structural mediator for heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Separate treatment of lattice and electronic transport provides the mechanism for improved prediction.
Incorporating Debye temperature contributes to the proposed transport-prediction mechanism.
Incorporating temperature-dependent lattice heat transport contributes to the proposed prediction mechanism.
The predictive approach is applicable from 200 K to 1200 K.
The approach is intended primarily for high-temperature applications.
HfNbTaTiZr has a total thermal conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m) from 300 K to 1200 K.
Earlier approaches use DFT-derived elastic properties and analytical conductivity estimates.
Understanding of atomic-scale complexity and separate transport behavior in HfNbTaTiZr is limited.
A deviation greater than 20% between predicted and experimental total conductivity falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims accurate separation of lattice and electronic transport, but the experiment measures only total conductivity, so it cannot determine whether the two components were predicted separately without compensating errors.

A claim of at least 20% improvement relative to earlier approaches is not equivalent to requiring less than 20% absolute deviation from experiment; the stated falsification rule therefore does not directly test the comparative improvement claim.
Applicability is claimed down to 200 K, but validation begins at 300 K, leaving the 200–299 K portion of the claimed range untested.
